name: Should I update my trim as a standalone project or during a full remodel?

mainEntity.name: Should I update my trim as a standalone project or during a full remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can upgrade trim as a standalone project, but completing it during a broader kitchen, bath, or drywall remodel is often more cost-effective. Removing old trim almost always damages adjacent drywall paper or exposes unpainted lines and uneven wall patches. If you plan to replace flooring, repaint rooms, or reconfigure wall openings in the future, timing your finish carpentry to coincide with those projects avoids paying twice for prep work, caulking, and paint touch-ups. At HH Remodeling, we frequently combine trim work with complete interior renovations.
acceptedAnswer.description: Combining trim installation with a remodel or flooring project saves labor, as removing older trim frequently requires drywall repair and paint touch-ups.
